title: Manuel Azuares (Carlist agent) to the Carlist Secretary of State: letter from London, partly in letter-substitution cipher, no. 780 (duplicate)
correspondents: Manuel Azuares -> encargado de la Primera Secretaria de Estado of the pretender Carlos V
folio_note: 12 pages, 12 images; cipher runs on image 3 (lines 2-3 of the text) and image 5 (six lines of letters)
status: PARES: 'La carta esta parcialmente cifrada' (news of the court of Maria II of Portugal after the Carlist success near Madrid). Images seen: cipher runs written in letters inside clear Spanish, plus some digit groups ('4607229'). No interlinear or marginal decipherment on the leaves seen (images 1-3, 5, 8 of 12); a duplicate copy, so the original may be elsewhere in the fonds.
why: Carlist foreign-agent correspondence of the First Carlist War in a letter cipher with clear context on both sides of every run, so cribs are plentiful (court of Maria II, Lisbon, Dona Maria de la Gloria). Sister of N.5 (same fonds, same year).
score_note: Images viewed 9 Nov 2026 (pares.cultura.gob.es, zoom 10): cipher confirmed on image 3 and image 5.
verify: Read all 12 images; compare with N.5 (Villafranca, St Petersburg, Aug 1837) and the other Carlist items of volume 161 (correspondencia carlista).
access_note: images online without login (PARES ViewImage.do, dbCode 30041306)
prior_art: open as far as checked (9 Nov 2026): known.py on the signatura, PARES id and correspondents finds nothing; two web searches (shelfmark / correspondents with cifra, cifrada, descifrada) found no edition, study or decipherment; PARES describes the cipher but gives no decipherment
source: Spain nobility / ACA sweep (PARES, AHN Diversos-Colecciones), 9 Nov 2026

seen.extent: Letter no. 780 (marked 'Duplicado') from London, 8 Sep 1837, 12 images. Cipher runs: 2 lines at top of image 3 plus a short group mid-page ('4607229' digits), a block of 7 lines on image 5, 3 lines at top of image 12, and one more run lower on image 12; several hundred letters in all.
seen.cipher: Monoalphabetic-looking letter substitution written in the same cursive hand as the Spanish text (letters g, h, l, n, p, u, v, y, z, o, c, e dominate), embedded in clear Spanish with a few digit groups for names. No decipherment, interlinear gloss or marginal plaintext on any leaf viewed.

prior_art.decode: Not found on DECODE: repo known.py search finds no DECODE record; a web search for DECODE/de-crypt.org plus Carlist 1837/1840/1875 returned only general DECODE pages (DECODE records need a login, so the live database was not queried).
prior_art.tomokiyo: No Cryptiana/Tomokiyo post on Carlist or 19th-century Spanish letter ciphers found (web search 'Tomokiyo cryptiana Carlist cipher'); only 1520s Spanish and French material turned up.
prior_art.lasry: No Lasry paper or GL.htm entry on Carlist-war ciphers found; his nearest 19th-century work is the Josse French cipher, unrelated.
prior_art.edition: No edition of the letter found; PARES gives only the catalogue description 'La carta esta parcialmente cifrada'.
prior_art.literature: No literature on Azuares's cipher or the AHN Diversos-Colecciones 161 Carlist papers found in two searches on the First Carlist War and Carlist agents in London; only general Carlist history surfaced.

vetting.key_check: No key found or held for Azuares's cipher; nothing on DECODE or in the repo. The N.5 sheet (lead 2422) is a long enciphered text in a different notation (dotted letters struck through), not a key table, so it is not a key for this letter; untested.
vetting.key_in_volume: None identified. Volume DIVERSOS-COLECCIONES 161 holds N.5 (Villafranca) with a cipher sheet that PARES says explains the key used; viewed, it is cipher text in a different script style and does not serve as a visible key for N.2. Untested against N.2.
vetting.duplicates: known.py on 'DIVERSOS-COLECCIONES,161', 'Azuares', 'Villafranca', 'Van Halen', 'Garcia Montes', 'Candalija', 'TORENO,C.71' found only these leads, the sweep files and unrelated targets (feuquieres, testi1630). Marked 'Duplicado' on the cover: another copy of no. 780 may exist elsewhere in the fonds; not found.
